info.description: Indian Crop Pest & Disease dataset (ICPD), field photos with polygon annotations

image_info.notes: Crop corrected from cotton to chilli. Puckered upward-curling leaves typical of leaf curl. No insects visible; vectors were reported by the field team. Virus not lab-confirmed.

Borer entry hole + frass at node and on side branch; larva not seen. Leaf miner reported but no mines visible. Hand in frame. Leaves not annotated (stem-focused image). Watermark cropped from original.

Small orange-brown insects on stem near node (ant-like; species not confirmed; not the borer). Dark marks on stem below node; cause unclear. No borer hole or frass seen. Leaf miner reported but no mines visible. Reddish patch on lower-left leaf is out of focus and not annotated. Hand and flower in frame.

Whole plant view. Reddish-brown damage at central node (probable borer entry); brown spot on side branch below node. Drooping shoot at top-right (possible borer wilt). Larva not seen. Leaf miner reported but no mines visible at this distance. Neighbouring plants overlap so no whole_plant polygon was drawn.

Plucked shoot held in hand. Stem split open at node with borer tunnel and frass; pinkish object inside the hole is possibly a shoot and fruit borer larva (needs a closer photo to confirm). Second hole with frass at top of side shoot; that shoot is wilted. Leaf miner reported but no mines visible.

White powdery spots across upper leaf surface (powdery mildew), heavier on upper-right and lower parts. Approx. 4 serpentine leaf miner trails visible (not reported by field team). Second infected leaf bottom-left. Same leaf as ICPD-000008 (duplicate_group RG-LEAF-01). Mildew marked as cluster regions, not individual spots.

Angular, vein-bounded yellow patches turning brown in the centre across most of the main leaf, typical of downy mildew. Not confirmed: an underside photo showing grey-purple sporulation is needed. Background leaves at top and right also affected. One small hole centre-right (cause unclear). Mildew marked as cluster regions, not individual patches.

Portrait photo of the same leaf as ICPD-000006 (duplicate_group RG-LEAF-01); keep both in the same split. White powdery spots across upper surface (powdery mildew). Approx. 4 serpentine leaf miner trails visible (not reported by field team). Second infected leaf bottom-left. Mildew marked as cluster regions.

Green boll top-left with dark purple-brown spots (probable boll rot / anthracnose). Leaves show red margins with brown necrosis and downward curl, consistent with jassid hopperburn; look-alikes: magnesium deficiency, late-season senescence. No bollworm or sucking pests visible. Open healthy bolls top-right. Background leaves blurred, not annotated.

Single green boll with scattered purple-brown spots and blotches (probable boll rot). Dried bracts on top. No pink bollworm entry or exit hole visible; damage from this pest is usually inside the boll and needs dissection to confirm. Background open bolls blurred, not annotated.

Compound tomato leaf over plastic mulch. Dry tan-brown papery patches at leaflet tips and margins. Could be early/late blight or Tuta absoluta blotch mines; they look alike in this photo, so marked unknown_symptom pending expert check (hold leaflet to light: mines show a hollow with frass inside). One small hole on right leaflet. No whitefly or mites visible. Strong sun and shadow. A small dry strip on the lower edge of the left leaflet is not annotated.

Whole staked tomato plant on plastic mulch wilting: lower and side leaves dried brown and drooping, stems yellowing; healthy plants behind (top-right) not annotated. Fusarium wilt vs bacterial wilt cannot be told from the photo: needs a stem cut (brown vascular ring) or ooze-in-water test. No pests reported.
